title: Running through 11/2 at MTC - also did I mention Victoria Clarkand Wi...
transcript: this Broadway show combines edge-of-your-seat drama with a sort of true story procedural element and ends up being emotionally devastating in the process this week I was invited to a special performance of Punch on Broadway followed by a talkback with some of the real people depicted in the play the play tells the story of a man who accidentally kiIIed someone with only one punch during a bar fight and it's told in a split perspective between him and the parents of the victim and they sort of converge as they both participate in a restorative justice program I knew going in that there was a bit of an activism component to it because the real people involved have been very vocal about these issues but I did worry that the play would end up being a little bit too preachy and to be honest it maybe does have its moments here and there but for the vast majority of it it's just a compelling story with beautiful character work and it culminates to a scene at the end that is sure to go down as one of the most tense and riveting scenes in the entire theatre season meanwhile the social importance of the play comes through pretty organically and don't get me wrong this does feel like a very important play especially in an age where we as a society seem almost less interested than ever in rehabilitation and forgiveness and I can even own up to some of that personally like I went into this with some skepticism after reading the description and being like “is this really the story we wanna be telling?” and I was even watching it with a lot of that same scrutiny about like whether it would end up being too forgiving of what he did in a way that would be disrespectful to the parents of the victim but it seemed like at every turn they rode that line perfectly and approached it with the level of nuance and complexity that this difficult topic warranted and any lingering doubts I might have had absolutely went away during the talkback when the real life parents basically pleaded to us to encourage as many people as possible to see this play

However, they note minor caveats about occasional preachiness, placing this at the top of the Positive range rather than full Rave.
